Remove listed animals from a pedigree

Source: R/removeAnimals.R
removeAnimals.Rd

removeAnimals() removes the rows of the listed animals and sets to NA each sire or dam entry that names one of them, so that no animal is left with a parent that has no row. An offspring of a removed animal keeps its other parent: one known parent is legal here. Afterwards checkPedigree reports none of the removed animals as rowlessParents, a parent with no row, which findGeneration cannot place and kinship cannot take.

Usage

removeAnimals(ped, ids)

Arguments

ped

a data frame with the columns id, sire and dam, an unknown parent written NA (see recodePedigree). Factor columns are read by their labels and numbers as text.

ids

a vector of the animals to remove, compared with id, sire and dam as text. An id need not have a row: a listed sire or dam with no row of its own is cleared from its offspring. An id found nowhere in ped is ignored, and NA among ids removes the rows whose id is NA.

Value

ped without the rows whose id is listed, and with each listed sire or dam set to NA; its other rows, in their order and with their row names, its columns and each column's type are unchanged.

Details

On the pedigrees its tests compare, the result equals kinship2's pedigree.trim() wherever that returns (it stops whenever an offspring would keep only one parent), and Pedixplorer's subset(del_parents = "one") except that Pedixplorer also clears the parent that is not removed.

See also

removeUnknownAnimals, removeUninformativeFounders, checkPedigree

Examples

## A and B have C and D; C and E have F and G; D and H have I.
ped <- data.frame(
  id = c("A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F", "G", "H", "I"),
  sire = c(NA, NA, "A", "A", NA, "C", "C", NA, "D"),
  dam = c(NA, NA, "B", "B", NA, "E", "E", NA, "H")
)
## Without C's row, C is a sire with no row of its own.
checkPedigree(ped[ped$id != "C", ])
#>            check id       detail
#> 1 rowlessParents  C sire of F, G
## removeAnimals() also clears C as the sire of F and G, who keep their
## dam E.
kept <- removeAnimals(ped, "C")
kept
#>   id sire  dam
#> 1  A <NA> <NA>
#> 2  B <NA> <NA>
#> 4  D    A    B
#> 5  E <NA> <NA>
#> 6  F <NA>    E
#> 7  G <NA>    E
#> 8  H <NA> <NA>
#> 9  I    D    H
checkPedigree(kept)
#> [1] check  id     detail
#> <0 rows> (or 0-length row.names)
gen <- findGeneration(kept$id, kept$sire, kept$dam)
kinship(kept$id, kept$sire, kept$dam, gen)["F", "G"]
#> [1] 0.125
